prompt:
A simulated brick world had this hidden rule:
In this world the agent's observation shows the target shifted: the target, missing, extra and target-height channels are rolled 4 columns toward higher x, wrapping around. The world, its designs and scoring are as described.

Below is what an AI scientist wrote during a search in that world: its analysis at every round, in order, and the
name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?
- "yes": it states the rule's substance (what is changed and how).
- "partly": it identifies the right kind of change but not its specifics.
- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no results yet. The starting architecture scored 0, and in 6 of 7 earlier worlds every trial scored a flat 0. That pattern suggests the world differs from its description, so in this round I change what the network assumes, not the recipe. Nothing is ruled out yet: action layout (symmetry, type order), DONE index, footprint/anchor convention and obs orientation are all open. All 6 candidates share one template. They read legality and layout from the mask reshaped under several layouts, decode outputs under the same layouts and sum them at full scale. If n_place ≠ T*Y*X, they fall back to a Linear embedding of the mask. All use the world-2 recipe. Each candidate isolates one hedge, plus one that combines them all, so any nonzero training success shows which deviation matters. With one seed, differences under about 0.07 may be noise.

### Round 2
All 6 round-1 trials scored 0, in training too. Parameter counts match the spec as described (Z=6, 4 types, 8x8, n_place=4*Y*X), so the mask-decode branch ran and the grid sizes are as stated. On one seed each, round 1 rules out these deviations: a 4- or 16-layout action indexing (8 grid symmetries × type-major/minor), DONE at index 0, an obs flipped or transposed relative to the actions, and anchor or footprint offsets within 2 cells. Any obs channel permutation is absorbed by the learned 1x1 stem. Still untested:
(a) action axis orders with the type in the middle (Y,T,X or X,T,Y);
(b) an obs whose memory layout is scrambled, such as channels-last data read as channels-first;
(c) non-local links between obs and actions, or non-local dynamics;
(d) an arbitrary action permutation.
This round tests each of these alone, on the world-2 recipe, plus two combinations. No recipe-only candidates.

### Round 3
All 12 trials score 0, and training success is 0 as well. The parameter counts match the stated spec exactly: r2c5's 382,362 parameters imply Y=X=8, n_place=256, n_actions=257, T=4 and Z=6. That rules out a wrong grid size or action count. Every other deviation tested so far has also failed, at least as far as summed hedges can learn it: obs/action orientation (all 8 symmetries and both type orders), any action-axis order, the obs memory order, DONE at index 0, footprints or anchors within a 5x5 window, coarse row/column context, and a dense per-action path. A reordering of obs channels is absorbed by the 1x1 stem anyway. Untested so far: arbitrary spatial remaps or shifts beyond 2 cells, a wrapping (toroidal) grid, different vertical dynamics, target/build misalignment under the full 8-symmetry set, and a harder-than-described world that limits learning by sample count. This round places one bet on each, plus one combined bet.

### Round 4
All 18 trials scored 0 on dev and in training. The parameter count of r1c1 (53,130) matches T=4, 8x8 and C=27 exactly, so the spec is as described and the conv layout path ran. The deviation lies in behaviour, not in sizes. These single deviations are ruled out at this budget: action axis order and flips (24 layouts), DONE at index 0, obs memory order, obs flips, transposes and rotations, wraparound, arbitrary cell remaps (mixer), per-layer reasoning, larger anchor offsets (5x5 head), and simply having more samples (1 epoch). Two kinds of deviation remain untested. One is scale: obs values or rewards far from 0/1. A huge reward would swamp the policy gradient in the shared trunk through the value loss. The other is reward shaping that is sparse or misleading, which could make the policy collapse onto DONE. This last round adds GroupNorm after the learned stem and a separate critic trunk to every candidate. It then varies horizon, entropy, update count and hedge width.

## Trial it ended with
name: norm+critic, 4x more updates
hypothesis: This is candidate 1 with 32 minibatches of 64 samples instead of 8 of 256, and lr 1e-3. That gives 4x more gradient steps at the same FLOPs, because FLOPs are charged per sample, not per update. It targets a world harder than described, where learning stalls before the first exact build within this budget. If it scores 0, an optimisation-speed bottleneck is refuted.

Return a JSON object: "verdict" ("yes", "partly" or "no") and "evidence" (at most 80 words, quoting the text and
naming the round it comes from).

reply.evidence: The text never says the target channels are shifted 4 columns with wraparound. Round 3 only lists "shifts beyond 2 cells, a wrapping (toroidal) grid... target/build misalignment" as separate untested options among many others. It never claims any of them is the rule. Round 4 then says "wraparound, arbitrary cell remaps (mixer)... larger anchor offsets" are "ruled out", and it moves on to reward and obs scaling. The idea of a misaligned target comes up only as a guess, and the text drops it.
